items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I heard Joe Venuti. He played at an outdoors pavilion. I was about half a block from him... And I told my mother, “That’s what I want to play.”

ctx.x: Tell me, you’ve been playing for a long time, a lot of great music, with a lot of great performers. What first attracted you to the guitar and the violin?

Well my brother-in-law was, knew quite a bit about strings and he started me out on, you know, we used to sit around the house and play old blues on guitar, and I’d watch him. And when he’d put the guitar down I’d pick it up and play blues. And he saw that I was interested, and he went and bought a mandolin and he would pick the melody on the mandolin and show me the changes on the guitar. So I actually played guitar. I got where I was pretty good but when he’d lay the mandolin down, I’d pick it up and play that.…
I wanted to ask you now, in some of those early days, the bands had string players is that right?
